case.title: An infrared flare in the galaxy NGC 3239 in 2020 that no optical survey saw: probably a very dusty nova
case.hook: Found blind by Oddsky's mid-infrared difference imaging of 318 nearby galaxies (hunt H-0012) and reported as AT 2020afkm: a flare peaking in 2020 November with no optical alert. Hubble caught a faint point source 85 days later that has since vanished, and JWST found warm dust at the same spot in 2024. K. De's group, who flagged it independently in 2022, favour a very dusty nova from a near-infrared spectrum taken during the outburst.
case.summary: A mid-infrared flare in the irregular galaxy NGC 3239 (about 8-12 Mpc), peaking in 2020 November at roughly 5e5 L_sun from ~960 K dust, that no optical survey reported. Hubble caught a faint, fading point source 85 days after the peak, and JWST found warm dust at the same spot in 2024. Reported to the IAU Transient Name Server as AT 2020afkm and described in AstroNote 2026-308. K. De's group (Columbia), who flagged it independently in 2022, favour a very dusty nova eruption from a near-infrared spectrum taken during the outburst. Found blind by Oddsky hunt H-0012.

claims.text: WISE (unWISE neo11 epochal coadds, difference imaging): flat from 2010 to 2020 May 2; on 2020 Nov 23 W1 +232 +- 8 and W2 +308 +- 20 uJy above the 2010-11 level; 91/119 uJy in 2021 Apr, 38/42 in 2021 Nov, ~27 in 2022 Apr. Position 156.29118 +17.16387 (Gaia-tied, ~0.25"). Positive in both visit seasons, so not an asteroid (hunts/H-0012/reviews/ngc3239-check-2026-11-01.md).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: The transient's W1-W2 is 0.95 +- 0.08 (~960 K dust); a blackbody gives ~5.6e5 L_sun at 7.9 Mpc (1.6-2.4x more at the 10-12 Mpc of SN 2012A's host distance and CosmicFlows-4). The rise is unresolved (< 205 d), so the true peak may be higher.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: HST (2021 Feb 16): a point source at 156.291224 +17.163778, 0.37" from the WISE centroid, F606W 25.93 +- 0.06 and F814W 24.95 +- 0.06 AB, present in all four 2021 exposures; absent in 2022 (F606W > 27.1) and in every 2025 filter, with no residual cluster (M_V > -2.9). The chance of an unrelated vanishing source within 0.37" is ~0.2%.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: JWST (programme 3707, 2024 Apr-May): a new unresolved source 0.01" from the HST position, F335M 5.9 uJy and F300M 3.2-3.6 uJy, nothing in F150W (> 26.5 AB): ~580 K dust at ~3.6e4 L_sun. Spitzer 2008 shows nothing there (> 8 sigma below the 2024 source).
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: No optical detection: no TNS object or ZTF alert; ATLAS limits o ~20.4-21.7 around the event; the galaxy was in solar conjunction in 2020 August. VLASS < 0.36 mJy (2021 Nov); Chandra 2025 < 2.6e37 erg/s.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not a buried normal supernova as it stands: the HST colour allows A_V <~ 2, while the faintness relative to WISE needs A_V 9-20, and an enshrouded Type II SN should be 30-100x brighter in the infrared at this phase. An obscured luminous red nova (stellar merger), an ILRT-like eruption (no progenitor seen), or a low-energy SN behind clumpy dust fit better. Not an AGN: 2.7 kpc from the centre of a galaxy with no nucleus.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Not reported (2026-11-01): TNS, Gaia alerts, CBAT, ATel (web search), SPIRITS, MIRONG, the literature; no publication on the JWST 3707 data at this position. ADS full-text check of the De et al. WISE transient papers still owed.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: ADS full text (2026-11-01, hunts/H-0012/work/ads_novelty.json): none of the 67 WISE/NEOWISE transient papers by De et al. and the SPIRITS papers mentions NGC 3239; the 59 papers mentioning NGC 3239 (or Arp 263, UGC 5637) with transient/infrared terms since 2020 are galaxy, ISM and morphology studies and the SN 2012A progenitor-disappearance study, none reporting a 2020 transient; coordinate searches find only unrelated papers. Apparently unreported.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Timing correction to C1/C2 from the TNS pre-filing check (hunts/H-0012/drafts/tns_OS-0030_validation.md, recompute_numbers.py): epoch times are now the mean of the NEOWISE exposures covering the source, not the tile-wide unWISE header midpoint. Last quiet epoch 2020-04-28 18:15 UT (MJD 58967.760; C1 said 2020 May 2); first detection 2020-11-23 16:30 UT (MJD 59176.688; earlier notes used 59176.37); later epochs 2021-04-30 and 2021-11-22. The rise is therefore unresolved within < 209 d (C2 said < 205 d). Forced photometry at the HST position gives W1 +231.8 +- 8.3 and W2 +310.0 +- 20.0 uJy at discovery (28 and 15.5 sigma) and 94/129 uJy on 2021-04-30, consistent with C1 within the errors. Published distances to NGC 3239 span 6.95-12.4 Mpc (NED, 12 values), so C2's luminosity scales accordingly.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Reported to the IAU Transient Name Server on 2026-11-02 by Alan Shortz (Oddsky) as AT 2020afkm (https://www.wis-tns.org/object/2020afkm; TNS ID 224693; internal name Oddsky OS-0030; AT type Other - Undefined), with the unWISE NEO11 credit line agreed in writing by A. Meisner. It was the only TNS object within 60" besides SN 2012A immediately before and after filing.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Published as TNS AstroNote 2026-308 on 2026-11-02 (https://www.wis-tns.org/astronotes/astronote/2026-308): 'AT 2020afkm: a dust-obscured infrared transient in NGC 3239 found in archival WISE data, with a fading Hubble counterpart and a JWST dust remnant', A. Shortz (Oddsky), with the full note as a PDF and Figures 1-4 attached.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: K. De (Columbia University; email to A. Shortz, 2026-11-02, permission given to note it publicly): his group independently flagged this source in 2022 in WISE data and obtained a near-infrared image and spectrum with ground-based telescopes during the outburst. Based on these they favour a very dusty nova eruption, consistent with the faint 2021 HST counterpart; the object is in their sample of nearby infrared transients. Noted on the TNS page of AT 2020afkm the same day. Oddsky's TNS report is the first public report, but De's group found it first.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A dust-obscured stellar eruption or merger (luminous red nova or ILRT-like event) in NGC 3239, peaking around 2020 November.
hypotheses.would_falsify: A JWST spectrum showing supernova signatures, or a late radio detection of a normal SN.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A low-energy or heavily, clumpily obscured core-collapse supernova whose dust is now cooling.
hypotheses.would_falsify: A spectrum of the remnant without supernova features.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A WISE, HST or JWST artifact, or an unrelated variable star.
hypotheses.would_falsify: Already falsified by three instruments at one position.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: A very dusty classical nova eruption in NGC 3239 (K. De et al., from a near-infrared spectrum during the outburst).
hypotheses.would_falsify: A published spectrum without nova features; still to be reconciled: the ~5e5 L_sun infrared luminosity at first detection and the ~3.6e4 L_sun dust source still present in 2024.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

args.reason: WISE, HST and JWST see the same unreported object at one position
An outburst spectrum (claim C12) favours a dusty nova over a red nova or ILRT.
An outburst spectrum (claim C12) favours a dusty nova; a buried supernova was already a poor fit.
